title: Animals, Objects, Fires & Potholes
citation: NJTR-1 Crash Report Manual (2023), Appendix: General Questions
key_points: Always complete an NJTR-1 for an animal strike; send it to NJDOT only if it's reportable.
A load or object falling off one vehicle onto another is a multi-vehicle non-collision crash.
Potholes and raised manhole covers count as fixed-object crashes.

faq.q: A car hits a dog. What report?
faq.a: An NJTR-1, every time. It goes to NJDOT only if it meets the reportable criteria; otherwise mark it non-reportable and keep it. Typical codes: contributing circumstance 57 – Animal in Roadway; Sequence of Events 24 – Deer or 25 – Other Animal. A horse pulling a buggy is not "an animal" for this purpose.

faq.q: A tire kicks up a rock that hits another car.
faq.a: Complete an NJTR-1, reportable or non-reportable based on your investigation and the criteria.

faq.q: Something falls off one vehicle and hits another.
A tree branch, golf ball or baseball hits a moving car.
faq.a: It can be classified as a one-vehicle non-collision crash.

faq.q: Why report potholes and manhole covers if they're temporary?
faq.a: They're fixed-object crashes, and the reports help find road maintenance and engineering problems.

faq.q: A car hits a parked, unhitched, registered trailer.
faq.a: A one-vehicle crash. The trailer is a non-fixed object; put its information in the narrative.

faq.q: Does a vehicle have to be moving for a fire to be an NJTR-1?
faq.a: Yes. A fire that starts in a vehicle in transport is a non-collision crash.

faq.q: A car runs onto a center island and needs a tow.
faq.a: Yes, an NJTR-1. Send it to NJDOT if it's reportable; keep it if not.

faq.q: A snowmobile hits a parked car.
faq.a: Yes, an NJTR-1. Snowmobile, ATV and dirt bike crashes with injury, death or property damage follow the same reporting rules (N.J.S.A. 39:3C-21).

faq.q: A riding mower hits a moving car, or a tree.
faq.a: Mower vs. a vehicle in transport: yes. Mower vs. a fixed object only: no.
